evidence: Clear directory-based modularity with well-defined packages (fsdet/, datasets/, tools/, demo/, configs/) and bounded contexts (e.g., fsdet/modeling, fsdet/evaluation, fsdet/data)

High cohesion within modules: fsdet/modeling contains core model components (RCNN, ROI heads), fsdet/evaluation contains dataset-specific evaluators, fsdet/data handles dataset registration and metadata
Low inter-module fan-out (avg 4.48) and shallow directory depth (max 4) indicate cohesive, loosely coupled modules
Centralized configuration via fsdet.config and shared engine/training/evaluation patterns in fsdet/engine and tools/
No evidence of network boundaries, separate processes, or service communication — all components run in a single Python process
Heavy internal reuse of detectron2 components via imports, but fsdet encapsulates domain-specific few-shot logic in its own modules
risks: Tight coupling to detectron2 internals may reduce portability
Monolithic deployment may limit scalability for distributed inference/training without external orchestration
Large fsdet module may grow into a god module if not carefully maintained
